correctness.rationale: For A any finite real symmetric n×n and g>0, each distinct eigenvalue theta gives 2×2 block [[theta,g],[g,0]] with lambda_(theta,±)=(theta±sqrt(theta²+4g²))/2. Both eigenvalue branches are strictly increasing, of opposite signs, hence no cross-theta collisions and full projectors E_theta ⊗ P_(theta,±). Cesàro phase averaging gives Mhat(H)=sum projectors Schur squared. Adding the two layer Schur squares yields one-half block [[S+Tg,S−Tg],[S−Tg,S+Tg]], S=sum E_theta∘E_theta and Tg=sum theta²/(theta²+4g²)(E_theta∘E_theta). Orthogonal layer transform gives S⊕Tg. Each Schur-square matrix is PSD, so ker Tg is intersection of ker Q_theta, theta!=0, invariant for all g>0; Tg decreases Loewner in g. H_g nonsingular, enabling iterated doubling. Path sine-square profiles independent up to reflection give path-comb rank m; clique projectors J/n,I−J/n give sharp min eigenvalue (n−2)/(n(1+4g²)) for n>=3. Independently diagonalized H_g for 4 matrices including singular bases at 3 couplings each, reproducing Schur block, rank and Loewner statements numerically to 1e−10. The analytic spectral derivation carries the unrestricted quantifiers.
risk: Uniform positive g required; g=0 has degenerate eigenspaces and can change rank.
Finite floating-point numerical checks are corroborative; no heterogeneous pendant-coupling assertion.

value.rationale: Uniform pendant coupling is a canonical graph transformation and long-time quantum average mixing rank is a natural transport invariant. A universal exact block decomposition, monotone mode damping without rank loss, infinite iterated doubling, half-rank path combs and sharp positive clique gap give reusable structure beyond tabulating a toy spectrum. Physical/graph significance is explicit and the result is not merely an evaluation of one parameter.
risk: Applies only to real symmetric A, uniform g>0 and infinite-time Cesàro mixing; excludes heterogeneous leaves and finite-time mixing.

limitations: Strictly positive uniform pendant coupling, all finite real symmetric A; distinct base eigenvalue projectors are grouped before averaging.
